key_finding: A closed-loop DT (moving-average lead-time forecast, simulation, ANN surrogates inside PSO) re-optimising SOUT parameters every 30 days kept fill rate near 99%, cut backlog by 81-92% and improved time-to-recover and time-to-survive versus static parameters under COVID-shaped lead-time disruptions, at ~8.7 s per review; no human step in the loop.

quotes.text: the proposed DT consists of the Physical System (PS), which represents the real-world production–distribution processes, and the digital counterpart, denoted as Cyber System (CS), which is the virtual replica of the PS.
Our focus is on the warehouse, which needs to issue orders to the supplier to satisfy the demand for raw materials from the production plant.

the CS consists of a combination of a simulation model, data analytics with the Moving Average (MA) technique, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as an ML model, and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) as a metaheuristic algorithm for the optimization procedure.
Then, the two surrogate models are integrated into a PSO metaheuristic to select the optimal replenishment parameters that minimize the provided objective function.
the digital twin learns from the real production–distribution data and periodically self-adjusts the replenishment parameters based on the evolution of the external environment.
The optimal triplet of parameters determined by the PSO is then utilized in the PS.
